title: Effectivity of etale algebraic-space descent along proper surjections
statement: Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Quasi-compactness of a space means that every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source. A space is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact, and a morphism is quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Etaleness means chartwise etaleness [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], which allows nonrepresentable maps. Finite presentation means local finite presentation on scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $p:B'\to B$ be a proper surjective morphism of finite presentation between quasi-separated algebraic spaces, where proper means separated, finite type and universally closed [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $X'\to B'$ be quasi-compact and chartwise etale with $X'$ quasi-separated. Give it an isomorphism $\theta:p_1^*X'\simeq p_2^*X'$ over $B'\times_BB'$ that restricts to the identity on the diagonal and satisfies $p_{23}^*\theta\circ p_{12}^*\theta=p_{13}^*\theta$ on the triple product. Then there exist a quasi-separated algebraic space $X$, a quasi-compact chartwise etale map $X\to B$, and an isomorphism $X\times_BB'\simeq X'$ inducing exactly $\theta$. No separatedness is imposed on $X'\to B'$, and no flatness is imposed on $p$.

source.place: Corollary (5.16), printed p.22; Notation (5.1), Remark (5.2), and the standing quasi-separatedness convention on printed p.4. The algebraic-space base extension is Remark (5.2). Read online; local copy WANTED. A stronger object-effectivity statement is Stacks spaces-pushouts.tex Tag 0GG0 (lemma-descend-etale-proper-surjective), read as a cross-check.

proof.text: Use the equivalence of [lem-sfb-space-etale-sheaf-realization]. Its explicit formula also checks base-change compatibility: for $g:H'\to H$ and a scheme $t:T\to H'$, both $E_{H'}(g^{-1}A)$ and $E_H(A)\times_HH'$ have sections $(t,s)$ with $s\in\Gamma(T,(gt)^{-1}A)$. The restriction maps agree by the composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Hence these spaces are naturally isomorphic. Applying the natural unit and counit gives $g^{-1}h_V\simeq h_{V\times_HH'}$, compatibly with maps and iterated pullback. Put $F=h_{X'}$ on $B'_{\mathrm{et}}$. The given $\theta$ therefore defines $\varphi:r_1^{-1}F\simeq r_2^{-1}F$ on $C=B'\times_BB'$, with exactly the same diagonal identity and triple cocycle. No representability of $X'\to B'$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 0GG0 (lemma-descend-etale-proper-surjective), first paragraph; Tag 0GF6, explicit realization functor and its natural unit/counit.

proof.text:
Write $r_1,r_2:C\to B'$ and $a=pr_1=pr_2$. Form the sheaf
$$G=\operatorname{Eq}\bigl(p_*F\rightrightarrows a_*r_2^{-1}F\bigr).$$
For the first arrow use the adjunction unit for $r_1$, followed by $\varphi$; for the second use the unit for $r_2$. Composition of direct images identifies their targets. Equalizers exist and are computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. Explicitly on an etale test $T\to B$, $G(T)$ consists of sections $s$ of $F$ over $B'\times_BT$ satisfying $\varphi(r_1^{-1}s)=r_2^{-1}s$ on $C\times_BT$. Evaluation on these possibly nonschematic spaces uses the enlarged-site equivalence and direct-image formula of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0GFW (lemma-glue-etale-sheaf-proper-surjective); explicit equalizer from etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0GF0, via the construction in Tag 0GEZ (lemma-glue-etale-sheaf-integral-surjective).

proof.text: Pull this equalizer back along $p$. Inverse image preserves finite limits by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism]. The maps $r_1,r_2$ are proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-set-sheaf-base-change] first to $p$ and then to $r_2$ to identify the two pulled-back terms with the direct-image terms for the base-changed datum over $B'$. These are the canonical counit mates, so applying adjunction to the two arrows gives respectively the pullback of $\varphi$ and the two projection units: their adjoints are the same restrictions of the original sections. Thus $p^{-1}G$ is the sheaf of matching sections for the pulled-back cover $q:B'\times_BB'\to B'$, where $q$ is the second projection. This cover has the diagonal section. In the next step we compute its equalizer rather than assume a sheaf-descent theorem.

source.place: Tag 0GF0, base-change of the equalizer; Tag 0DG0 (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), applied to p and to the projection r_2.

proof.text: Here is the split-cover calculation, on every etale test $T\to B'$; write $x_0:T\to B'$ for its fixed structure map and $x_1$ for the variable coordinate on $B'\times_BT$. A matching section $s$ lies in the pullback of $F$ by $x_1$; matching means $\varphi_{12}(s_1)=s_2$ on the double overlap. Restrict $s$ along the diagonal $x_1=x_0$ to obtain $t\in F(T)$. Conversely send $t$ to $s=\varphi_{01}(t)$, with $t$ first pulled back from $T$. The identity $\varphi_{12}\varphi_{01}=\varphi_{02}$ proves matching. Pulling matching back along $(x_1,x_2)=(x_0,x_1)$ proves $s=\varphi_{01}(t)$; the diagonal identity proves the other composite is the identity. These restrictions commute with every test map. The sectionwise criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] gives an isomorphism $\alpha:p^{-1}G\simeq F$. On $B'\times_BB'$, the same matching identity says that evaluating a family at the second distinguished coordinate is $\varphi$ times evaluation at the first. Therefore $r_2^{-1}\alpha\circ c=\varphi\circ r_1^{-1}\alpha$, where $c$ is the canonical overlap map for $p^{-1}G$. This verifies the prescribed datum, not only the existence of an isomorphic underlying sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0GG0, compatibility with the descent datum; expanded split-cover equalizer verification in etale-cohomology.tex Tags 0GEY and 0GEZ.

proof.text: Choose a common universe bound containing the small site and its set of generator/section pairs for $G$, as allowed by [def-weil-size-convention] and the explicit size convention in [lem-sfb-space-etale-sheaf-realization]. This is a set: $G$ is the sectionwise equalizer of two set-valued sheaves on a small skeleton. Form $X=E_B(G)$. The realization node gives a chartwise etale algebraic space $X\to B$. Its natural unit, the base-change identity of step 1, $\alpha$, and its natural counit give $X\times_BB'\simeq X'$. The overlap equation at the end of step 4, and full faithfulness of that equivalence, imply that the induced space isomorphism is exactly $\theta$.

source.place: Tag 0GG0, realization and set-theoretic footnote; Tag 0GF6 (lemma-sheaf-gives-space), size condition.

proof.text: For an affine scheme $T\to B$, put $T'=B'\times_BT$. It is quasi-compact because $p$ is proper (hence quasi-compact), with base change as in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The hypothesis on $X'\to B'$ uses affine tests, so convert it to the quasi-compact space $T'$: choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to T'$ with $U$ quasi-compact and write $U=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ with $U_i$ affine open. Each $X'\times_{B'}U_i$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis, and $\coprod_iX'\times_{B'}U_i\to X'\times_{B'}T'$ is surjective on points by the image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Its point map is continuous, so $X'\times_{B'}T'$ is quasi-compact. The same argument shows in general that a morphism quasi-compact on affine tests is quasi-compact on all quasi-compact space tests; the converse is trivial. Thus the affine-test convention of the statement agrees with the quasi-compact-space convention of [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local, lem-sfb-space-quasiseparated-test-calculus]. The map $X'\times_{B'}T'\to X\times_BT$ is surjective: it is the base change of $p$, and [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives surjectivity after every base change as well as continuity. A continuous surjective image of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact: pull any open cover back, take a finite subcover and use surjectivity. Thus $X\times_BT$ is quasi-compact for every affine $T$, proving that $X\to B$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 040W (lemma-surjection-from-quasi-compact) and Tag 03HE (definition-quasi-compact), written open-cover and affine-test conversion; retention of quasi-compactness as in Rydh (5.16).

proof.text: The relative diagonal $\Delta_{X'/B'}$ is the base change of the absolute diagonal of $X'$ along $X'\times_{B'}X'\to X'\times_{\mathbf Z}X'$. It is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local], whose quasi-compact-space convention agrees with the affine-test one by step 6. For an affine scheme $T\to X\times_BX$, set $D=T\times_{X\times_BX}X$. Put $T'=T\times_BB'$, which is quasi-compact as in step 6. The space $D'=T'\times_{X'\times_{B'}X'}X'$ is quasi-compact by quasi-compactness of $\Delta_{X'/B'}$, tested on the quasi-compact space $T'$ as allowed by step 6. Fibre-product identities identify it with $D\times_BB'$. Its map to $D$ is surjective and continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The same open-cover argument makes $D$ quasi-compact. Hence $\Delta_{X/B}$ is quasi-compact. Finally [lem-sfb-space-quasiseparated-test-calculus] composes the quasi-separated morphisms $X\to B$ and $B\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, making $X$ absolutely quasi-separated. The arguments include empty bases and empty etale objects and impose neither flatness on $p$ nor separatedness on $X'\to B'$.

source.place: Tags 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact) and 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), diagonal and open-cover verification; quasi-separatedness convention of Rydh (5.16).
